fullPassage: In the past, being a fan of a Korean pop idol typically meant waving colored balloons at concerts and sending gifts. Most fans, often teenagers, admired their idols from a distance. However, over the past three decades, the K-pop fandom culture has evolved dramatically with the development of digital technology. Today, fans actively engage themselves in communication with their idols through social media platforms. They can provide feedback and suggestions, which can have a beneficial influence on their idols. When they see some positive changes in their idols, they feel rewarded for their contribution. In other words, fans have changed from consumers to active participants in the K-pop phenomenon. In addition to this change in their attitudes and roles, today’s fans express their affection in different ways. Instead of showering their idols with material gifts, they organize fundraising and volunteer activities in the name of their idols. For example, fans of a popular idol group have raised funds to support children’s charities. Fans’ efforts not only promote good images of their idols but also foster the value of sharing. This change in fandom culture shows how fans’ interaction with K-pop idols has become more dynamic and meaningful. The new culture brings fans closer to their idols and provides a more inclusive and rewarding experience for them.
title: The Changing Face of K-Pop Fandom
